Introduction:

Wherever human beings live, besides mutual help and cooperation, the existence of differences is also a natural matter. A dispute can arise between two human beings. Disputes can arise within a family or tribe, and conflicts are born among compatriots. In the same way the arising of differences and conflicts between countries is also a natural matter. In the world the first and second World Wars and the wars between countries also began because of conflicts to obtain resources and domination etc. Conflicts keep arising, but countries can also resolve these conflicts through mutual consultation, thought and the best practical strategy.

Historical Background of the Existing International Conflicts

1. Palestine Dispute

Modern Palestine is that region of the Middle East which is spread from the Mediterranean Sea to the River Jordan and from Lebanon to the Sinai peninsula of Egypt. In 1917 the Palestinian region went from Turkey into the control of Britain. In that same period a world organisation of the Jews was started by the name of Zionism, whose aim was to bring together the Jews spread across the world and establish a state named Israel in the Palestinian region. Britain too had announced support for this aim. Despite clear Arab opposition the Jews began to come into the Palestinian areas, and by 1947 about 19 lakh Jews had settled here. In that same year the United Nations decided that this region be divided into two states, i.e. Palestine and Israel, and that Bait-ul-Muqaddas (Jerusalem) would be given under world control. Israel accepted this decision, but the Arabs strongly opposed the division of the region. In this way on 14 May 1948 the establishment of the Israeli state was announced.

At the time of the establishment of Israel, 35 percent Jews and 65 percent Palestinians lived in this region. The Arab world did not accept the existence of Israel, and in the Arab–Israeli war of 1948-49 the Arabs were defeated. Israel occupied the new city of Jerusalem and half the region of Palestine. Jordan occupied the old Jerusalem and the West Bank of the River Jordan, while Egypt occupied the Gaza Strip. In the year 1967 a six-day war took place between the Arabs and Israel, in which Israel occupied the West Bank of the River Jordan, the Gaza Strip and East Jerusalem. Because of this the Palestinians were scattered. About ten lakh became citizens of Israel, twenty-nine lakh are in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, and about fifty lakh took refuge in Jordan, Lebanon, Syria and other Arab countries. During this period small battles kept taking place between Palestinian mujahideen and Israelis. Indescribable cruelty was inflicted on the Palestinian people, and Western countries kept supporting Israel. On 13 September 1993, at Oslo, an agreement was made between the head of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO), Yasser Arafat, and the Israeli government. In some areas of the Gaza Strip and the West Bank a Palestinian government was established in the name of the Palestinian National Authority. But in exchange for this the PLO also recognised Israel, with which the Palestinian mujahideen became angry, and under the leadership of the organisation named Hamas they pledged an armed struggle to eliminate Israel and establish a Palestinian state. Later, talks continued between the PLO and Israel until 2010 for a permanent solution, but no satisfactory result came out, and in this way the future of the Oslo agreement is also in danger. However, for the resolution of this issue both parties are busy in negotiations, and whatever is seen in the form of the Palestinian National Authority is the fruit of these negotiations.

2. Afghan Dispute

Afghan history is full of wars. The present Afghan conflict began at that time when on eleventh September 2001 air attacks took place on the World Trade Center New York and the Pentagon of America, in which, besides financial loss, thousands of people also died. America claimed that an extremist Muslim organisation, al-Qaeda, did this, whose leadership was at that time the guest of the Taliban government in Afghanistan. America made two demands of the Taliban head of state, Mullah Muhammad Omar: to close all the centres of al-Qaeda in Afghanistan and to hand over the leadership of al-Qaeda, especially Osama bin Laden, to America. اِسرائیل کے قیام کے وقت اِس علاقے میں 35 فیصد یہودی اور 65 فی صد فلسطینی آباد تھے۔ اِسرائیل کے وجود کو عرب دُنیا نے تسلیم نہیں کیا اور 1948-49ء میں عرب اِسرائیلی جنگ میں عربوں کو شکست ہوئی۔ اِسرائیل نے یروشلم کے نئے شہر اور فلسطین کے آدھے علاقے پر قبضہ کیا۔ اُردن نے پرانے یروشلم اور دریائے اُردن کے مغربی کنارے جبکہ مصر نے غزہ کی پٹی پر قبضہ کیا۔ سال 1967ء میں عرب اور اِسرائیل کے درمیان چھ دن کی جنگ ہوئی جس میں اِسرائیل نے دریائے اُردن کا مغربی کنارہ، غزہ کی پٹی اور مشرقی یروشلم پر قبضہ کیا۔ اِس سے فلسطینی بکھر گئے۔ دس لاکھ کے قریب اِسرائیل کے شہری بنے، اُنتیس لاکھ مغربی کنارے اور غزہ کی پٹی میں اور پچاس لاکھ کے قریب اُردن، لبنان، شام اور دیگر عرب ممالک میں پناہ گزین ہوئے۔ اِس دوران فلسطینی مجاہدین اور اِسرائیلیوں کے درمیان چھوٹی موٹی لڑائیاں ہوتی رہیں۔ فلسطینی عوام پر ناقابلِ بیان ظلم کئے گئے اور مغربی ممالک اِسرائیل کا ساتھ دیتے رہے۔ 13 ستمبر 1993ء کو اوسلو کے مقام پر آزادیٔ فلسطین کی تنظیم (Palestine Liberation Organization-PLO) کے سربراہ یاسر عرفات اور اِسرائیلی حکومت کے درمیان معاہدہ ہوا۔ غزہ کی پٹی اور مغربی کنارے کے کچھ علاقے میں فلسطین نیشنل اتھارٹی کے نام پر اپنی حکومت قائم کی گئی۔ لیکن اِس کے بدلے پی ایل او نے اِسرائیل کو بھی تسلیم کیا جس سے فلسطینی مجاہدین ناراض ہوئے اور اُنہوں نے حماس نامی تنظیم کے زیرِ قیادت اِسرائیل کو مٹانے اور فلسطینی ریاست کے قیام کیلئے مسلح جدوجہد کا عہد کیا ہے۔ بعد میں مستقل حل کیلئے پی ایل او اور اِسرائیل کے درمیان بات چیت 2010ء تک جاری رہی لیکن کوئی خاطر خواہ نتیجہ نہیں نکلا اور اِس طرح اوسلو معاہدہ کا مستقبل بھی خطرے میں ہے۔ تاہم اِس مسئلے کے حل کیلئے فریقین گفت و شنید میں مصروف ہیں اور جو کچھ فلسطینی قومی اتھارٹی کی شکل میں نظر آ رہا ہے یہ گفت و شنید کا ثمر ہے۔
